data.householdPolicy: Adult men only; no minors, no women, no couples.
data.operatorNotes: Faith-based shelter averaging 170+ stays per day across shelter plus transitional beds. Intake gate includes breathalyzer screening at the door and chapel attendance expected during stay — in practice this filters out roughly a third of would-be intakes with active substance use. Storm surge has pushed occupancy higher overnight; intake gate conditions unchanged.

data.householdPolicy: Daytime drop-in only; site has no overnight beds. CURRENTLY OFFLINE.
data.operatorNotes: CURVEBALL STATUS: Storm damage forced emergency roof repair; daytime hub closed 48-72 hours. Walk-in services temporarily relocated to Center of Hope at reduced hours. The highest-volume walk-in intake in the system (80-120 contacts/day) is offline during the surge window.

data.householdPolicy: Unaccompanied youth only; Drop-In Center serves anyone age 24 or younger.
data.operatorNotes: CURVEBALL STATUS: Absorbed 3 youth displaced by the overnight storm; 1 of 12 beds remaining. DCF has flagged 4 additional transition-age foster youth with disrupted placements expected to present within 72 hours, which would push the site into overflow. Community's only 24-hour low-barrier youth shelter. Accepts self-referral, law-enforcement drop-off, agency referral.

data.householdPolicy: Unaccompanied youth; parenting youth with one child accepted.
data.operatorNotes: CURVEBALL STATUS: At full occupancy with no vacancy. The only transitional-housing downstream option for CrossRoads exits is unavailable for the duration of the storm surge. Apartment-style transitional living for youth aging out of foster care or escaping homelessness. Up to 18 months stays. Active case plan required.

data.householdPolicy: Families with at least one minor child; no single adults.
data.operatorNotes: Storm-surge intakes pushed family-shelter occupancy close to capacity. 90-day stay limit, entry only through 211 coordinated screening or partner-agency referral. Background-check blockers unchanged; any recent adult felony conviction still bounces the whole family back into the queue.

data.householdPolicy: Families with children; scattered-site host-congregation and apartment model.
data.operatorNotes: Capacity counted in families, not beds. Hosted one additional family overnight through the host-congregation rotation. Employment-readiness eligibility unchanged, which continues to filter out some of the displaced families arriving from the Red Cross activation.

data.householdPolicy: Singles and families served through parallel programs, not combined.
data.operatorNotes: Transitional housing plus rapid-rehousing rental assistance. Referrals flow through coordinated entry. Emergency financial-assistance program receiving heavy demand this morning from households whose landlords declared apartments uninhabitable after the storm.

data.householdPolicy: Referral and resource hub, not a shelter — no beds on site.
data.operatorNotes: On-site staff absorbing the Open Door overflow while its hub is offline. HMIS integration still not live, so coordinated-entry workflow is still phone-based — a significant bottleneck given the current surge volume.

data.householdPolicy: Singles and families in permanent supportive housing units.
data.operatorNotes: Permanent supportive housing — occupancy unchanged by the storm event because admissions happen on the coordinated-entry waitlist timeline, not real-time. Housing First model, rent at 30% of income. 8-12 week waitlist remains the system's dominant bottleneck on the permanent-housing side.

data.providerName: Mental Health Association of South Central Kansas
data.householdPolicy: Adults with serious mental illness; singles only.
data.operatorNotes: Occupancy unchanged. COMCARE clinical-assessment requirement adds 2-4 weeks to any new intake; during a surge like this, that referral path is effectively closed to anyone without an active clinical record.
